name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Syntax-check every .cjs / .js
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          for f in **/*.cjs **/*.js; do
            case "$f" in node_modules/*) continue;; esac
            node --check "$f"
          done
      - name: Install (no secrets required)
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund || true
      - name: Test (runs against the zero-dependency echo path)
        run: npm test

# Prompt Engineer — Architecture

Prompt Engineer is the discipline layer for prompts an agent writes for itself. Every prompt is scored on six dimensions (specificity, depth, generativity, self-evolution, originality, grounding), and one below the rubric floor is REJECTED, not saved — the gate is real, not decoration. An anti-pattern scan catches the failure modes of self-authored prompts: repeating the same category, grandiosity with no concrete actions, obesity, and self-congratulation with no adversarial challenge. Approved prompts are auto-versioned, indexed, and linked into a parent→child genealogy, and a surfacing ranker picks the next one to run by quality × recency so good new prompts aren't starved and old great ones don't rot. Pure Node, zero dependencies; categories, patterns, and the rubric floor are all configurable, and a deterministic demo runs the whole loop with no API key.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    W["a machine-authored prompt"] --> SC["SCORE\n6-dim rubric"]
    SC --> G{"avg >= floor?"}
    G -- no --> REJ["REJECT\n(throws w/ rubric)"]
    G -- yes --> AP["anti-pattern scan"]
    AP --> V["version + index"]
    V --> GEN[("genealogy\nparent -> child")]
    V --> SURF["surface next\nquality x recency"]
    classDef acc fill:#4a3617,stroke:#E0A356,color:#fff;
    class SC acc;
    class G acc;
    class SURF acc;
```

## How it fits together

Prompt Engineer is a registry + quality gate for machine-authored prompts, built as a `PromptEngine` class with everything configurable (categories, patterns, triggers, rubric floor, grounding-reference list) and self-contained state under ./data. score(text) returns six 0–10 dimensions — specificity (concrete action verbs), depthPotential (recursive/meta cues), generativity (open questions), selfEvolution (version/iterate markers), originality (novelty markers), grounding (references to the named context resources) — plus an average and a passes flag. register(opts) is the gate: it scores, runs checkAntiPatterns() over the recent index, and if avg < rubricFloor it throws a RUBRIC_FLOOR error with the rubric attached (unless rubricOverride is set) — so a sub-threshold prompt is never saved. Approved prompts get a metadata header, an auto-versioned filename, an append to the JSONL index + a Markdown generation log, and — when a parent_id is given — a parent→child genealogy edge. surfaceOne() ranks unexecuted prompts by rubric average plus a recency bonus (1.5/(1+ageDays/7)) so fresh-good beats stale and old-great stays warm; markExecuted() records outcomes; stats() summarizes the library. Every disk write is guarded; a failure is logged, not fatal. The CLI exposes score/stats/next/list.

## Extending it

Every capability is a self-contained module. To add your own, follow the contract the existing
modules use and wire it into the entry point. Keep it portable — config via `.env`, no hardcoded
paths, no personal accounts.

## Design principles

1. **The gate is real.** A prompt below the rubric floor is refused, not saved. A quality bar you can bypass by default is decoration; this one throws.
2. **Name the failure modes.** Self-authored prompts drift in specific ways — comfort-zone, grandiosity, obesity, self-congratulation. Detect them explicitly instead of hoping.
3. **Evolve, don't sprawl.** Every prompt is versioned and linked to its parent, so a library becomes a genealogy you can reason about rather than a pile of files.
4. **Yours to define.** Categories, patterns, triggers, the floor, and what counts as grounding are all configuration — the machinery is generic, the taxonomy is yours.

what it does

A rubric with teeth.

01 / SCORE + GATE

Six dimensions, one floor

Every prompt is scored 0–10 on specificity, depth potential, generativity, self-evolution, originality, and grounding (references to the context resources you name). The average is checked against a floor you set — below it, `register()` throws with the rubric attached instead of saving. Pass an explicit override only when you're testing the rubric itself. The bar is enforced, not suggested.

02 / ANTI-PATTERNS

The way self-authored prompts fail

A scan over the recent history catches the specific failure modes: the same category four times in the last ten (comfort-zone), fewer than five concrete action verbs behind grand language (grandiosity), thousands of words that should have been split (obesity), and confident assertions with zero adversarial challenge (self-congratulation). Findings are recorded on the entry, not silently dropped.

03 / VERSION + TRACE

A library that evolves

Approved prompts are auto-versioned and indexed as append-only JSONL, with a parent→child genealogy so you can see which prompt spawned which. A surfacing ranker picks the next prompt to run by quality × a recency bonus — a fresh-but-good prompt isn't starved by a stale one, and an old-but-great one stays warm. Everything is a file you can read.

quickstart

Up and running in a clone.

Every value comes from .env. Nothing here is tied to any account — bring your own.

# 1. no install needed — pure Node builtins
node examples/demo.cjs                 # register + score + gate + genealogy, end to end

# 2. score any prompt text from the CLI
node lib/prompt-engineer.cjs score "identify, build, and measure ..."
node lib/prompt-engineer.cjs stats     # library stats
node lib/prompt-engineer.cjs next      # the next prompt to run

# 3. in your code
#   const { PromptEngine } = require('./lib/prompt-engineer.cjs');
#   const pe = new PromptEngine({ dataDir: './data', rubricFloor: 7 });
#   const entry = pe.register({ name, category, content, trigger, primary_pattern, parent_id });
